name: Jane Fraser

career.title: Consultant, rising to partner (financial services and global strategy)
Head of client strategy, then Global Head of Strategy and M&A
CEO of Citi Private Bank, then CitiMortgage, then U.S. Consumer and Commercial Banking
President and CEO of Global Consumer Banking
CEO (also Chair of the Board from October 2025)

background_rationale: Spent a decade at McKinsey, rising to partner in its financial services and global strategy practice, before joining Citi as a strategy executive and then running a series of its businesses.

notable.summary: Announced plans to eliminate about 20,000 jobs, roughly 10% of Citi's workforce, by 2026 as part of a reorganization to simplify the bank.
Citi agreed to sell a 25% stake in its Mexican unit Banamex to businessman Fernando Chico Pardo for about $2.3 billion, ahead of a planned public listing.
Fraser was elected Chair of Citigroup's board in addition to her role as CEO.
At Citi's May 7, 2026 investor day, Fraser's team set a target of a 14% to 15% return on tangible common equity by 2031, which some analysts said fell short of expectations.

personal_story.hook: A St Andrews schoolgirl who earned pocket money caddying became the first woman to run a major U.S. bank.
personal_story.summary: Fraser was born in 1967 in St Andrews, Scotland, an only child whose father was an accountant, and as a schoolgirl earned pocket money caddying on the town's Old Course; she spent part of her teenage years in Australia. She considered medicine before deciding her strengths lay in economics, which she studied at Cambridge, then worked as an M&A analyst at Goldman Sachs in London and at a brokerage in Madrid, where she became fluent in Spanish. After a Harvard MBA she spent a decade at McKinsey, making partner while working part-time as a mother of two young sons. A 1999 book she co-authored on global strategy caught the eye of Citi executive Michael Klein, who spent years recruiting her; she joined Citi in 2004 and in 2021 became the first woman to lead a major U.S. bank.

Exact Banamex sale stake/closing details: the 25% sale to Chico Pardo was announced Sept 2025 and reportedly closed Dec 2025; a further ~24% sale has also been reported but not verified here.
